key_insight: The paper turns neural-operator CFD surrogates into reliability-aware predictors by adding conformal calibration that provides calibrated uncertainty for both vehicle-level drag and spatial surface fields.
engineering_relevance: This enables aerodynamic designers to quickly identify which vehicle geometries and surface regions need expensive CFD verification, improving surrogate-based design iteration decisions.
method: GeoTransolver serves as the main neural-operator surrogate, with Transolver used to test transfer across architectures.
Drag coefficient uncertainty is calibrated using conformalized quantile regression to produce case-level prediction intervals.
Pressure and wall shear stress use point prediction plus residual-scale modeling and residual-normalized conformal calibration for spatially adaptive intervals.
evidence_signal: Across split and cross-validation-assisted out-of-fold protocols at 90% nominal coverage, out-of-fold aggregation reduced drag-interval coverage variability from 10.41 to 3.10 percentage points and cut mean surface-field interval widths by 22.68% for pressure and 25.35%–27.09% for WSS.
watch_item: Conformal reliability depends on the calibration protocol and data distribution, so coverage may weaken under strong dataset shift or if residual-scale estimation is poorly regularized.
paper_title: Multi-Granularity Conformal Prediction for Reliable Neural-Operator Automotive Aerodynamic Surrogates
